title: Sampling Is Not Curiosity: Why LLM Agents Should Investigate
why_read: This paper makes a precise and useful distinction between stochastic sampling and genuine curiosity-driven exploration in LLM agents, which matters for anyone designing agentic systems.
analysis: The core argument is that LLM agents don't truly explore their environment. They sample from a fixed probability distribution conditioned on context, which is fundamentally different from the kind of curiosity that drives action in reinforcement learning. Real curiosity, as defined in the RL literature, requires a model that updates based on new interactions, persists across context windows, and actively seeks out information that reduces its own uncertainty. The paper proposes a formal framework for what genuine curiosity would require in an LLM agent and identifies open research directions needed to build it.
